mainEntity.name: How do I decide between converting a garage and building a new home addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A garage conversion is often ideal if you want to add living space without sacrificing yard area or altering your home's exterior footprint. You gain enclosed square footage quickly, but you give up covered vehicle parking and traditional garage storage. In contrast, a bump-out addition preserves your garage but consumes outdoor yard space and requires new foundation pouring, exterior roofing, and matching siding or stucco. Homeowners must compare their need for vehicle and tool storage against their willingness to reduce lawn size.
acceptedAnswer.description: Converting a garage saves yard space and uses existing framing but eliminates parking, whereas a bump-out addition preserves the garage while expanding onto your lawn.
